root_cause: Escape key pressed inside the dropdown triggers Dropdown.dataApiKeydownHandler, which calls event.stopPropagation(). This prevents the event from bubbling up to the modal's escape handler, so the modal does not close when focus is on the access toggle button.
repair_strategy: Modify Dropdown.dataApiKeydownHandler to conditionally stopPropagation only for non‑Escape keys. Keep event.preventDefault() to avoid default actions, but allow Escape to propagate so parent containers (e.g., modal) can handle it and close themselves.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will now close the share dialog when focus is on the access toggle button, providing a keyboard‑only way to dismiss the modal and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard accessibility.
functional_risks: Escape key inside a dropdown may also close an ancillary modal or dialog that was not intended to be dismissed by Escape in that context.
If a custom component relies on the dropdown swallowing Escape, its behavior could change.
verification_requirements: Pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle button closes the share dialog and returns focus to the Share button.
Dropdown still closes when Escape is pressed and focus returns to the toggle button when the dropdown is not inside a modal.
ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter keyboard navigation inside the dropdown continues to work as expected.
Modal keyboard escape handling remains functional for other focus positions inside the modal.
